about: Built by tools/build_economy.py from data/records.json, data/interiors.json and research/facts.json.

trades.note: Businesses named in the clearance claims (GRS HKRS1255), counted once each; the trade is classified by us from the business name. 'unknown' means the name gives no trade.

floors.note: Floors named in business claims; a claim can name more than one floor.

tiles.label: Rent compared with the rest of Kowloon (1974)

facts.claim: Monthly room rent
sources: Adolfo Arranz, 'City of anarchy' (graphic), South China Morning Post, 16 Mar 2013, p. A18

facts.claim: A whole unit rented for about $800 a month in 1979
sources: HK01 series 真．城寨英雄 (parts 1-3), 26-28 Aug 2016: members of the Walled City kaifong association remember

facts.claim: Rents were about a third below the rest of Kowloon (government housing was cheaper still)
sources: House of Lords debate 'Walled City of Kowloon', HL Deb 11 June 1974 vol 352 cc463-76 (Lord Kennet, Earl Cowley, Lord Goronwy-Roberts)

facts.claim: No rates, ground tax or real-estate tax were paid
sources: J.L. Battenfeld, 'Walled City a place of myths and crime', UPI, 18 Dec 1984
HK01 series 真．城寨英雄 (parts 1-3), 26-28 Aug 2016: members of the Walled City kaifong association remember

facts.claim: There were no land deeds: sales were recorded on handwritten receipts, witnessed and stamped by the kaifong association
sources: HK01 series 真．城寨英雄 (parts 1-3), 26-28 Aug 2016: members of the Walled City kaifong association remember

facts.claim: Compensation totalled about HK$2.7 billion (US$350 million), roughly HK$82,000 per person
sources: Wikipedia, 'Kowloon Walled City'
Teoalida, 'Kowloon Walled City'

facts.claim: Clearance claimant case files kept by the Government Records Service
facts.value: 8,823 files: about 7,900 household claims, 690 business claims, 85 property-owner claims
sources: HKSAR Government Records Service, series HKRS1255 'Case files relating to claimants of Kowloon Walled City clearance' (catalogue, 8,823 files)

facts.claim: Towers were built without architects or engineers, outside building and sanitation rules; many had poor or no foundations
sources: Adolfo Arranz, 'City of anarchy' (graphic), South China Morning Post, 16 Mar 2013, p. A18
Wikipedia, 'Kowloon Walled City'
House of Lords debate 'Walled City of Kowloon', HL Deb 11 June 1974 vol 352 cc463-76 (Lord Kennet, Earl Cowley, Lord Goronwy-Roberts)
J.L. Battenfeld, 'Walled City a place of myths and crime', UPI, 18 Dec 1984

facts.claim: 77 wells, some about 90 m deep; electric pumps lifted water to big rooftop tanks, and narrow pipes fed it down to homes
sources: Adolfo Arranz, 'City of anarchy' (graphic), South China Morning Post, 16 Mar 2013, p. A18

facts.claim: Eight freshwater standpipes: one inside the city and seven around its perimeter
sources: Adolfo Arranz, 'City of anarchy' (graphic), South China Morning Post, 16 Mar 2013, p. A18
Wikipedia, 'Kowloon Walled City'

facts.claim: Street taps stood only at the outer edge, on Tung Tau Tsuen Road and Tung Tsing Road; piping into the city was judged infeasible
sources: HK01 series 真．城寨英雄 (parts 1-3), 26-28 Aug 2016: members of the Walled City kaifong association remember

facts.claim: Young people carried water for elderly residents for 50 cents a load
sources: HK01 series 真．城寨英雄 (parts 1-3), 26-28 Aug 2016: members of the Walled City kaifong association remember

facts.claim: Plastic water pipes ran across the alleys and leaked; residents carried umbrellas against the drips
sources: Adolfo Arranz, 'City of anarchy' (graphic), South China Morning Post, 16 Mar 2013, p. A18
HK01 series 真．城寨英雄 (parts 1-3), 26-28 Aug 2016: members of the Walled City kaifong association remember
Robert Benjamin, 'Denizens of noted hellhole face Walled City eviction', Baltimore Sun, 30 Jun 1992

facts.claim: Light and power were taken from the mains by illegal connections; bare cables hung in festoons over the alleys
sources: House of Lords debate 'Walled City of Kowloon', HL Deb 11 June 1974 vol 352 cc463-76 (Lord Kennet, Earl Cowley, Lord Goronwy-Roberts)

facts.claim: The kaifong association arranged meters with the power company and residents helped run the wiring; broken cables were left and new ones added, shading the lanes
sources: HK01 series 真．城寨英雄 (parts 1-3), 26-28 Aug 2016: members of the Walled City kaifong association remember
This House (YouTube), 'The Densest City in Human History: A Rare Look Inside Kowloon Walled City', 28 Apr 2026, 12:20

facts.claim: Fluorescent tubes lit the lanes around the clock because daylight rarely reached street level
sources: Wikipedia, 'Kowloon Walled City'
This House (YouTube), 'The Densest City in Human History: A Rare Look Inside Kowloon Walled City', 28 Apr 2026, 12:20
Robert Benjamin, 'Denizens of noted hellhole face Walled City eviction', Baltimore Sun, 30 Jun 1992

facts.claim: With no proper collection, bulky rubbish (TVs, furniture, mattresses) was hauled up and dumped on the roofs
sources: Adolfo Arranz, 'City of anarchy' (graphic), South China Morning Post, 16 Mar 2013, p. A18
Wikipedia, 'Kowloon Walled City'

facts.claim: Government services in 1974: a sweeping team, refuse bins, public latrines, pest control, ditches cleared twice daily since 1973, pumphouses being installed
sources: House of Lords debate 'Walled City of Kowloon', HL Deb 11 June 1974 vol 352 cc463-76 (Lord Kennet, Earl Cowley, Lord Goronwy-Roberts)

facts.claim: Fish balls, barbecued and roast meat and other foods were made in premises with little or no sanitation
sources: Adolfo Arranz, 'City of anarchy' (graphic), South China Morning Post, 16 Mar 2013, p. A18

facts.claim: Fish ball factories were unlicensed and ran round the clock
sources: LCSD, Kowloon Walled City Park exhibition guide (the 'Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In' set exhibition)

facts.claim: Popular claim that up to 80% of Hong Kong's fish balls came from the city
sources: This House (YouTube), 'The Densest City in Human History: A Rare Look Inside Kowloon Walled City', 28 Apr 2026, 12:20

facts.claim: Businesses named in the clearance claims, by trade (classified by us from their names)
facts.value: 565 named businesses: 75 stores/trading, 74 food factories, 52 dentists, 44 plastics, 35 metalwork, 33 clinics, 28 leather/shoes/bags, 25 textiles, 20 restaurants, 15 electrical, 9 roast meat, 101 trade unclear
sources: HKSAR Government Records Service, series HKRS1255 'Case files relating to claimants of Kowloon Walled City clearance' (catalogue, 8,823 files)
